_note: Fifteen deep-coverage parks (seven original + eight promoted 2026-09-19). Shape: Omit<Park, 'id' | 'updated_at'> & { sources: string[] }. Coordinates are the spring vent / swim area (USGS spring sites), not park polygon centroids. typical_closure_time is the local time the park TYPICALLY fills on summer weekends and holidays (from official 'often reaches capacity' language plus news/visitor reports) and must be labelled as typical, never as live. usgs_site_id = gauge at/for the spring; river_gauge_site_id = nearby river gauge used when the spring has no live series or for river-driven brown-outs; gauge_distance_km = distance from the swim area to river_gauge_site_id when set, otherwise to usgs_site_id. nws_grid/nws_zone/nws_county fetched live from api.weather.gov/points on 2026-09-19. Facts verified against official pages 2026-09-18/19.

parks.name: Ichetucknee Springs State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. to sundown, 365 days a year. Swimming (North Entrance): Head Spring closes 30 minutes before park closing; Blue Hole Spring and its trail close 1 hour before closing. Tubing (South Entrance): Dampier's Landing closes 5 p.m., tube rentals end 4:30 p.m., everyone off the river by 6 p.m. Midpoint Launch closed for repairs.
parks.fees: $6 per vehicle (2-8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle or motorcycle; $2 pedestrians, cyclists and extra passengers. Tube rentals are extra through the concessionaire (about $10-$35).

rules.alcohol: Prohibited on the river and anywhere inside the park.
rules.tubing: Year-round from Dampier's Landing (South Entrance) only; the north section is closed to tubing. Tubes up to 60 inches, no glitter; stay on your flotation device; no swimming from tubes on the river.
rules.pets: Not allowed in the water, on trails to launches or swim areas, or in vessels. Trestle Point and Pine Ridge trails are pet-friendly.
rules.life_jackets: Allowed and rentable; pool noodles are fine in the springs but not on the river.
other: Swim only at the Head Spring and Blue Hole - no swimming anywhere on the river.
No coolers, food, disposables, glass, speakers, tobacco or vapes, water guns, DPVs or large inflatables at swim areas or on the water (armbands OK).
Scuba at Blue Hole only, cavern or cave certified, two-diver minimum, done one hour before sunset.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard on duty - swim at your own risk. The spring water is about 72 F year-round, cold enough to tire swimmers quickly. Blue Hole is deep with a strong current and is for experienced swimmers only; the stairs can be slippery. The Blue Hole vent is a cave - diving is for cavern/cave-certified divers only.
parks.entrance_notes: Two entrances. North Entrance (8294 SW Elim Church Rd, Fort White) is for swimming at the Head Spring and Blue Hole - no tubing. South Entrance (12087 SW US Hwy 27) is for tubing from Dampier's Landing - no swimming. Entry is first-come, first-served; online passes do not guarantee entry or skip the line. When the park is full it closes to everyone, including pass holders; do not park and wait on the roadside - citations are issued. Third-party reports: arrive before 10 a.m. on summer weekends.
parks.description: A crystal-clear, spring-fed river in north Florida where you can swim at the Head Spring and Blue Hole or float the river from the South Entrance. On hot weekends and holidays the parking areas fill early and the gates close until space opens up.

parks.name: Ginnie Springs
parks.hours: Mon-Thu 8 a.m.-5 p.m.; Fri-Sat 8 a.m.-7 p.m.; Sun 8 a.m.-6 p.m. Day passes stop being issued at 3 p.m. and expire at sunset. Divers register by 5 p.m. (4 p.m. in winter).
parks.fees: Day admission: adults $25 (Mar-Oct) or $20 (Nov-Feb); children 4-12 $6 or $5; age 3 and under free. Certified divers $36; full-cave divers $28. Tubes $10 single / $20 double per day; snorkel mask or fins $8 each; life jackets free.

rules.alcohol: Open containers only inside campsites (policy effective Apr 21, 2026). Prohibited at the springs, decks, swimming areas, bathhouses and picnic areas. No glass bottles anywhere on the property.
rules.tubing: Float the Santa Fe River from Beaver's Landing to Twin Spring (about 1 hour), then a 15-minute walk back. Free air-fill station.
other: Every guest signs a waiver.
Visitors under 16 need constant adult supervision; campers under 18 need a guardian.
Snorkelers on the river must tow a dive flag or float (state law).
No solo diving; divers must register and sign the dive waiver.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguards on duty - swim at your own risk. The water is about 72 F year-round. Ginnie's springs open into the Devil's cave system: cave diving is only for certified cave divers, and open-water divers may not carry lights or enter any overhead environment (an iron grate closes the Ginnie Ballroom cavern after past diver deaths). Santa Fe River currents can be strong and the water dark after rain.
parks.entrance_notes: Private park at 5000 NE 60th Ave, High Springs (386-454-7188). Day passes can be bought online - encouraged but not required. Admissions are limited under the park's safety policy and late arrivals are not guaranteed entry; day guests park in overflow lots on busy summer weekends. Third-party reports say it rarely sells out, so no typical fill time is listed.
parks.description: A privately run springs park on the Santa Fe River with several clear blue spring pools, sun decks and stairs with railings into the water. Popular with snorkelers, tubers and cave divers; it charges per person rather than per car.

parks.name: Poe Springs Park
parks.hours: Open 7 days. May-Sep 8 a.m.-8 p.m.; Oct-Mar 8 a.m.-5 p.m. (April hours are not published). The spring and boat ramp close 30 minutes before the park. Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day.
parks.fees: May-Sep: $6 per vehicle, or $1 per person for walk-ins and cyclists. Oct-Mar: free.

rules.alcohol: Not stated on the county page - ask at the gate.
rules.tubing: Tube rentals on the river through the park concessionaire (Anderson's Outdoor Adventures).
rules.pets: Allowed on a hand-held leash at all times; pets may not swim in the spring.
rules.life_jackets: Not stated on the county page.
other: The park may close when the spring reaches its capacity of 100 people.
Scuba diving is not permitted.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard statement is published - assume no lifeguard on duty. Spring water is about 72 F. The spring pool opens onto the Santa Fe River, which runs high, fast and murky after heavy rain; the swim area closes whenever water clarity is poor. Entry is by concrete steps with a handrail.
parks.entrance_notes: Alachua County park at 28800 NW 182nd Ave, High Springs (352-264-6847). No reservations. The designated swim area has been closed since Jul 16, 2026 (poor water clarity; the spring stopped flowing during the 2026 drought); picnic areas, trails, the boat launch and paddling remain open. With only 100 people allowed in the spring it can fill late morning on summer weekends when open.
parks.description: A small Alachua County park where a spring pool meets the Santa Fe River, with a lodge, pavilions and a boardwalk through cypress swamp. Cheaper and quieter than the state parks, but the swim area closes whenever the river backs up or clarity drops.

parks.name: Ruth B. Kirby Gilchrist Blue Springs State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. to sundown, 365 days a year.
parks.fees: $6 per vehicle (2-8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians and cyclists. Camping $18 per night plus fees.

rules.tubing: Not offered; rentals and concessions are unavailable during renovations.
rules.pets: Not allowed in swimming areas or the water (state park rule).
other: Snorkeling only in designated areas.
Registered campers may enter after the gate closes at capacity; day visitors may not.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard statement is published - assume no lifeguard on duty. Spring water is about 72 F year-round. The spring run is shallow and clear, but the Santa Fe River can back up into the springs and turn them dark after heavy rain.
parks.entrance_notes: Entrance at 7450 NE 60th St, High Springs (386-454-1369). No day-use reservations. On busy weekends the gate closes at capacity and does not reopen to day visitors until 8 a.m. the next day (visitor and county reports). Since Oct 29, 2025 there are no water activities while a new swim entrance, launch, bathrooms and larger campground are built - no reopening date yet.
parks.description: A group of clear springs on the Santa Fe River that became a state park in 2017, known for a wide, shallow run and easy snorkeling. The swimming area is closed for renovations until further notice; the picnic area and pavilion stay open.

parks.name: Rainbow Springs State Park
parks.hours: Headsprings (swimming) entrance: 8 a.m. to sunset, 365 days a year, unless closed at capacity. Tubing entrance: Memorial Day-Labor Day daily 8 a.m.-4 p.m. (last tram 4:30 p.m.); weekends only in spring and September (call to confirm); closed Oct-Mar.
parks.fees: $5 per vehicle (2-8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians and cyclists. Tube rental and shuttle fees are extra, and the shuttle fee applies even with your own tube. Annual passes are sold on weekdays and non-holidays only.

rules.tubing: Not allowed at the headsprings. Tubing only from the separate Tubing Entrance (2-mile float, about 2 hours); tubers must be 5 or older, and ages 5-6 must wear a fastened life jacket.
rules.pets: Welcome in the campground; not permitted in swimming areas or buildings.
rules.life_jackets: Life preservers and noodles are allowed at the headsprings; required for tubers ages 5-6.
other: No inflatables of any kind (rafts, tubes, balls) at the headsprings.
Stay inside the buoyed swim area; snorkeling only inside the buoys (dive-flag law applies elsewhere).
No disposable food or drink containers on the river (aquatic preserve).
Private vessels must be carried about 1,800 ft from parking to the launch.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard on duty - all swimmers do so at their own risk. The water is about 72 F year-round. The headsprings swim area is 10-18 feet deep with no shallow end, so weak swimmers should wear a life preserver and everyone must stay inside the buoys. Paths around the springs are steep and uneven in places.
parks.entrance_notes: Three entrances. Main/headsprings (swimming) entrance at 19158 SW 81st Place Rd, Dunnellon requires a day-use reservation for everyone, including annual passholders, pedestrians and cyclists. Tubing entrance at 10830 SW 180th Ave Rd (seasonal). Campground at 18185 SW 94th St. When the headsprings reach capacity the park closes to all visitors and vehicles may not wait in line in the park or on adjacent roads. Parking lot renovation Sep 9, 2026 - Feb 4, 2027: limited parking. Third-party reports: typically hits capacity 9-10 a.m. on summer weekends.
parks.description: A first-magnitude spring near Dunnellon with a deep, clear swimming basin surrounded by gardens and man-made waterfalls from its roadside-attraction days. Reservations are now required for the headsprings entrance, and on summer weekends it still reaches capacity early.

parks.name: Blue Spring State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. until sundown, 365 days a year. Swimming season is April 1 - November 14; the spring run is closed to swimming and all water activities November 15 - March 31 for manatees (reopening can be delayed if manatees linger).
parks.fees: $6 per vehicle (2-8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians, cyclists and extra passengers. Entry fee is collected online with the day-use reservation. Tube rentals extra (Blue Springs Adventures). Camping $24 per night; cabins $95 per night.

rules.tubing: Allowed in season; enter at the upper entry and float about 1/8 mile to the main swim dock. Inflatables over 72 inches are not allowed.
rules.pets: Pets - including service animals - are not allowed on the water.
other: No coolers, food, glass, speakers, tobacco, water guns or DPVs on the water.
No climbing the spring banks; no paddling in the swim area 10 a.m.-5 p.m.
Swimming with or approaching manatees is prohibited; no swimming after hours.
Scuba only in designated areas; open-water and free divers may not carry lights or go below 60 ft; 32 divers at a time; two-diver minimum.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard statement is published - assume no lifeguard on duty. The water is about 72 F year-round. The spring boil is deep and leads into a cave system below 60 ft (certified divers only, no lights for open-water divers); the run has a steady current toward the St. Johns River. Manatees use the run in winter - never approach or swim with them.
parks.entrance_notes: 2100 W French Ave, Orange City (386-775-3663). Day-use reservations required since Jul 15, 2026 for everyone except campers and boat-tour guests; news reports put the daily cap at about 232 vehicle and 50 pedestrian/bike slots (estimate). The park frequently reaches capacity and may close for several hours; pedestrians and cyclists are not admitted while it is closed. Third-party reports: closed by about 10 a.m. on summer weekends.

swim_season.note: Manatee season Nov 15 - Mar 31: swimming and all water activities in the spring run are prohibited. Reopening may be delayed if manatees linger.

parks.description: A first-magnitude spring on the St. Johns River south of DeLand, famous for wintering manatees and a clear quarter-mile spring run for swimming and tubing. Swimming is only open April 1 - November 14, and day-use reservations are required.

parks.name: Wekiwa Springs State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. to sunset, 365 days a year. The swimming area is open from 8 a.m. until 30 minutes before park closing. Spring bathrooms may close briefly for cleaning; concession 9 a.m.-5 p.m.
parks.fees: $6 per vehicle (up to 8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians, cyclists and extra passengers. The entry fee is collected online when you make the day-use reservation (no extra reservation fee). Camping $24 per night plus fees.

rules.alcohol: Prohibited (stated on the park's picnicking page and F.A.C. 62D-2.014).
rules.tubing: Not offered at the spring; individual-size flotation devices are allowed in the swimming area.
rules.pets: Allowed on a 6-foot hand-held leash on trails and in use areas; not allowed in the swimming area.
rules.life_jackets: Allowed; not required. Children and non-swimmers must be with an adult swimmer at all times.
other: No diving or jumping - the spring is shallow.
No scuba, hookah or other tank-assisted breathing systems.
Swimming and snorkeling only in the spring - not in Wekiwa Springs Run, Rock Springs Run or the Wekiva River.
No grills, pop-up tents or canopies on the spring lawn.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguards on duty - swimmers and snorkelers do so at their own risk. The water is 72 F year-round. The swim area is shallow (under 1 ft to about 5 ft), so diving and jumping are banned; the spring vent drops into a small cavern and scuba is prohibited. Children and non-swimmers must stay with an adult swimmer. Black bears and alligators live in the park.
parks.entrance_notes: 1800 Wekiwa Circle, Apopka (407-553-4348), off I-4 exit 94 about 20 minutes north of downtown Orlando. Day-use reservations are required for everyone, including annual passholders (since Sep 2, 2025); the daily number of reservations equals park capacity and same-day slots sell out on hot weekends and holidays. Ask the ranger station for a re-entry ticket if you leave. Campground construction may be under way (notice effective Jun 26, 2026).
parks.description: A large spring-fed swimming lagoon just north of Orlando, ringed by a grassy lawn for picnics and the start of the Wekiva River paddling trail. It is one of the few state-park springs with a swim lift and ramp into the water, and day-use entry now runs on reservations.

parks.name: Madison Blue Spring State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. to sunset, 365 days a year. Swimming hours are 8 a.m. to sunset; all dives must be completed one hour before sunset.
parks.fees: $4-$5 per vehicle ($5 for 2-8 people, $4 single-occupant); $2 pedestrians, bicyclists and extra passengers. Pay with the QR code at the entrance (honor system). No tube rentals in the park.

rules.alcohol: Prohibited in all areas of the park (stated on the official swimming and picnicking pages).
rules.tubing: Inflatable floats and tubes are allowed in the spring and the adjacent river - bring your own (no rentals). Tubes may not exceed 60 inches in more than one direction; no motorized equipment; no food, drink, pets, tobacco, alcohol or disposable items on the water.
rules.pets: Picnic areas only, on a 6-foot hand-held leash. Not permitted in the spring, the adjacent river or any building. Service animals are not allowed in the swimming areas (public bathing place).
rules.life_jackets: Allowed; not required. There is no lifeguard, so monitor inexperienced swimmers closely.
other: No climbing on, walking on, or jumping or diving from the limestone rocks around the spring.
Fishing and tobacco are banned in and around the spring; river fishing only from 400 ft past the spring.
Scuba is for cave/cavern-certified divers only - no open-water or free diving; two-diver minimum; sign in at the boardwalk; no DPVs; dives done one hour before sunset.
Vessels are not allowed in the spring or spring run, and there is no river launch in the park.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard on duty - swim at your own risk and watch inexperienced swimmers closely. The water averages 72 F year-round. The spring is about 82 ft wide and up to 25 ft deep, with wading areas under 5 ft. The vent opens into one of the largest cave systems in the area - cave/cavern-certified divers only. The Withlacoochee River can rise and darken the spring after heavy rain. Alligators sometimes visit the swim area.
parks.entrance_notes: 8300 NE State Road 6, Lee (850-815-0869), between Lee and Jasper. No reservations; pay by QR code at the gate. Official notice: the park experiences frequent closures between 10 a.m. and 3 p.m. on weekends and holidays due to high visitation - it closes at capacity and may reopen later the same day. Do not park and wait on the roadside or in the entrance area; local law enforcement issues citations. Temporary restrooms only, no bathhouse or changing area. Large RVs and trailers are not recommended (limited turnaround space).
parks.description: A first-magnitude spring in a limestone basin on the west bank of the Withlacoochee River near Lee, once voted the best swimming hole in the country. On summer weekends it closes at capacity as early as 10 a.m., so plan an early start.

parks.name: Lafayette Blue Springs State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. to sundown, 365 days a year. Divers register at the north entrance ranger station and must finish one hour before sundown.
parks.fees: $5 per vehicle (2-8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians, bicyclists and extra passengers. Honor box - correct change required. Cabins $100 per night plus fees; walk-in camping currently unavailable.

rules.tubing: Not offered and no rentals in the park. Suwannee River outfitters nearby (Suwannee River Rendezvous 386-294-2510, Camp Suwannee River Outfitters 386-647-6624) rent canoes.
rules.pets: Dogs on a 6-foot hand-held leash; not permitted in the springs, cabins or buildings; may not be left unattended more than 30 minutes.
other: Fishing is prohibited in the swim areas.

Scuba is cave diving only (Blue Springs and Green Sink) for certified teams of two or more; open-water diving is prohibited; no DPVs; register and show certification at the north entrance ranger station.
Day use, the spring and the ranger station are at the north entrance; the boat ramp and cabins are at the south entrance.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard on duty - swim at your own risk. The spring is 72 F year-round. The vent leads into the Green Sink cave system (over 12,000 ft surveyed) - certified cave divers only. The Suwannee River floods roughly one year in five and can back dark water into the spring (a brown-out); the swim area closes when the river is high or clarity is poor. A natural limestone bridge crosses the spring run.
parks.entrance_notes: North (day-use and spring) entrance at 799 NW Blue Spring Rd, Mayo (386-294-3667); the south entrance has the boat ramp and cabins. Honor-box entry, no reservations, first-come, first-served. The park publishes no capacity-closure pattern, so no typical fill time is listed. Check river levels before driving out - swimming closes when the Suwannee floods the spring.
parks.description: A quiet first-magnitude spring on the Suwannee River near Mayo, crossed by a natural limestone bridge and shaded by moss-hung oaks, with stilt cabins above the river. It rarely fills, but the swim area closes whenever the river backs up into the spring.

parks.name: Troy Spring State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. to sundown, 365 days a year. All dives must be completed one hour before sundown.
parks.fees: $5 per vehicle (up to 8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians, bicyclists and extra passengers. Honor box - correct change required.

rules.tubing: Not offered; no rentals or tube launch.
rules.pets: Dogs on a 6-foot hand-held leash; not permitted in the spring or buildings; may not be left unattended more than 30 minutes. Service animals are allowed in all areas.
other: Fishing only from the river bank or river dock - never in the swim area.
Scuba is open-water only for certified divers: no solo diving, no lights, no DPVs; show your certification; dives done one hour before sunset.
The remains of the steamboat Madison in the spring run are protected - do not disturb them.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard on duty - swim at your own risk. The spring is 72 F year-round and drops to about 70 ft at the vent, with shallow areas in the spring run for children. The Suwannee River can brown out the spring after heavy rain; swimming is not allowed when the spring is browned out or the river rises over the lower dock platform (park guidance). The dock is reached by a long paved switchback ramp.
parks.entrance_notes: 674 NE Troy Springs Rd, Branford (386-935-4835). Honor-box entry, no reservations. A small park that publishes no capacity-closure pattern, so no typical fill time is listed. Check the park page or call before driving out in wet weather - the spring closes to swimming when the Suwannee floods it.
parks.description: A 70-foot-deep first-magnitude spring on the Suwannee River near Branford, with the ribs of the Civil War steamboat Madison visible in the shallow spring run. A quiet alternative to the bigger springs, reached by a paved switchback ramp down to a dock.

parks.name: Fanning Springs State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. to sundown, 365 days a year. Divers must register three hours before sunset and finish one hour before sunset.
parks.fees: $6 per vehicle (up to 8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians, bicyclists and extra passengers; $2 per person arriving by boat (honor box on the dock). Cabins $100 per night plus fees.

rules.tubing: No tube run or rentals. Individual floats and rafts are allowed in the swim area (max 5 x 5 ft round or 4 x 6 ft rectangle).
rules.pets: Dogs on a 6-foot leash; not permitted in the swimming areas, cabins or buildings.
other: Fishing from the swimming dock is prohibited; no cast nets.
Open-water scuba in the designated swim area only: certified, register with staff, two-diver minimum, no lights; capacity 15 divers at a time and 30 per day.
Idle speed in the spring run - manatees use it in cooler months; stay 50 ft from manatees.
No outside firewood (emerald ash borer).

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard statement is published - assume no lifeguard on duty. The spring is 72 F year-round and only 18-21 ft at its deepest, with a shallow area for toddlers; wade in from the shore or dock. The Suwannee River is right beside the spring and backs dark water into it after heavy rain, which closes swimming. Manatees may be in the spring run in cooler months - keep 50 ft away. The floating dock is being improved (from Aug 20, 2026) and swimmers may be asked to exit at any time.
parks.entrance_notes: 18020 NW Highway 19, Fanning Springs (352-463-3420), right off US 19/98 at the Suwannee River bridge; boaters can enter from the river ($2 per person). No reservations; first-come, first-served. The park publishes no capacity-closure pattern, so no typical fill time is listed. Effective Aug 20, 2026 the floating dock is under improvement - swimming and boating stay open but be prepared to exit when asked.
parks.description: A second-magnitude spring (first-magnitude until the 1990s) beside the Suwannee River in Fanning Springs, with a shallow blue-green basin, a cypress-swamp boardwalk and riverfront cabins. Easy in-and-out swimming from the shore or dock, though the river can darken the spring after rain.

parks.name: Manatee Springs State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. to sundown, 365 days a year. Divers must register at the office by 3 p.m. and be out of the water one hour before sunset.
parks.fees: $6 per vehicle (2-8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle or motorcycle; $2 pedestrians, bicyclists and extra passengers. Diving is free with admission. Camping $20 per night plus fees.

rules.tubing: Not offered; no tube run or rentals. Swimming is only in the main spring basin.
rules.pets: Dogs on a 6-foot leash; not permitted in buildings or the swim area, and banned from all boardwalks. Leashed pets may wade in the spring run at the canoe launch.
other: Swimming and free diving only in the main spring - prohibited in Catfish Hotel, the spring run and at the end of the boardwalk.
Scuba: open-water in the main spring and Catfish Hotel; cavern at Catfish Hotel; full-cave certification for Friedman Sink. 18 open-water/cavern divers at a time; register by 3 p.m.
Keep 50 ft from manatees.
No bicycles on the boardwalk; no outside firewood; no EV charging in the park.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard statement is published - assume no lifeguard on duty. The spring is 72 F year-round. Use caution - the current in the spring is swift (official). The vent and the nearby Catfish Hotel sink lead into a cave system: cave-certified divers only, and Catfish Hotel is closed to swimming. Manatees gather in the spring run in cooler months - never approach them. The Suwannee River can flood back into the spring after heavy rain and close swimming.
parks.entrance_notes: 11650 NW 115 St, Chiefland (352-493-6072), about 6 miles west of US 19. No day-use reservations; first-come, first-served. The park publishes no capacity-closure pattern, so no typical fill time is listed. Effective Jan 14, 2026 the waterfront restroom and dump station are closed and no EV charging is allowed. Boaters can tie up at the river dock and walk the 800-ft boardwalk to the spring.
parks.description: A first-magnitude spring near Chiefland that sends about 100 million gallons a day down a short run to the Suwannee River, with an 800-foot boardwalk through cypress forest. Manatees use the run in winter; swimmers stay in the main spring basin.

parks.name: De Leon Springs State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. until sunset, 365 days a year. Swimming 8 a.m. until 30 minutes before sunset. Old Sugar Mill Pancake House 8 a.m.-4 p.m. daily; boat house, rentals and visitor center run 9 a.m.-6 p.m. during spring break (Mar 14-22) and summer (May 30-Aug 9).
parks.fees: $6 per vehicle (2-8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle or motorcycle; $2 pedestrians, bicyclists and extra passengers. Canoe/kayak/paddleboard rentals and the 50-minute boat tour are extra (Guest Services).

rules.alcohol: Not permitted in any area of the park (stated on the official swimming and picnicking pages).
rules.tubing: Not offered. Individual floats and rafts are allowed in the swim area (max 5 x 5 ft round or 4 x 6 ft rectangle).
rules.pets: Hand-held 6-foot leash at all times; not allowed in the sunbathing/swimming area; may not be left unattended. Service animals are allowed in all areas.
rules.life_jackets: Allowed; not required. Children and non-swimmers must stay with an adult swimmer inside the roped-off areas.
other: No swimming or snorkeling in Spring Garden Run (boats and alligators).
No recreational scuba - instructional diving only with a permitted instructor; no free-diving into the spring cave.
The swimming area closes when lightning is detected within 6 miles.
Artifacts in the spring are protected by state law; no metal detectors.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguards on duty - swim at your own risk. The water is a constant 72 F. Depths range from 18 inches to 30 ft at the spring boil, where a cave opens - free-diving into it is prohibited. Children and non-swimmers must be with an adult swimmer and stay inside the roped-off areas. Alligators live in Spring Garden Run, which is closed to swimming. The swim area closes when lightning is within 6 miles.
parks.entrance_notes: 601 Ponce De Leon Blvd, De Leon Springs (386-985-4212), north of DeLand. No day-use reservations; first-come, first-served. Visitor reviews report the park at capacity on hot weekends (June 2026), but the park publishes no typical fill time, so none is listed. Pavilions cannot be reserved April 1 through Labor Day weekend. Expect a wait for the pancake house on weekends.
parks.description: A spring-fed swimming basin north of DeLand, walled like a pool and famous for the Old Spanish Sugar Mill pancake house beside the water. One of the easiest springs to get into, with stairs, handrails and a swimmer chair lift.
sources: https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/site/?format=rdb&siteType=SP&siteStatus=all&bBox=-81.45,29.05,-81.28,29.22 (02236110 Ponce de Leon Springs is inactive - no IV series)

parks.name: Weeki Wachee Springs State Park
parks.hours: 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. daily, year-round (concessionaire-run). Buccaneer Bay beach and swimming are open daily; water slides close 4:30 p.m. and swimming 5 p.m. Slides and lazy river run daily May 23-Aug 8, 2026, weekends only Mar 24-May 22 and Aug 9-Sep 30, 2026, and daily Mar 14-23 (spring break).
parks.fees: $13 adults; $8 children 6-12; ages 5 and under free (covers the mermaid shows, river cruise and Buccaneer Bay). Lazy-river tube wristbands, beach chairs, cabanas and kayak rentals are extra.

rules.alcohol: No glass or alcohol inside the park.
rules.tubing: Personal tubes and rafts are not permitted (child floats and pool noodles are fine). Tubes rented from the concessionaire are used on the lazy river - riders must be 42 in. or taller, one rider per tube.
rules.life_jackets: Allowed in the swim area; not allowed on the water slides (nor masks, goggles or cameras).
other: Coolers 45 quarts or smaller; no grilling, pop-up tents, tables of food, chafing dishes or personal speakers.
Slides: 48 in. minimum height for Cannonball, 42 in. for Pirate's Revenge; no swimwear with buckles or rivets and no denim on slides.
No refunds or return tickets for weather closures; attractions can close for lightning.
Lil' Mates kiddie pool is closed for renovations (2026).

parks.safety_notes: Certified lifeguards are on duty at Buccaneer Bay (concessionaire statement). The spring is about 72-74 F year-round. The spring vent is the deepest known freshwater cave system in the United States - no public diving or entering the cave. The swim area is a natural spring with a current toward the Weeki Wachee River; the beach and slides close for lightning and no refunds are issued.
parks.entrance_notes: 6131 Commercial Way (US 19 at SR 50), Weeki Wachee (352-610-5660). Run by concessionaire Guest Services; per-person admission at the gate, no reservation required. In summer the park often reaches capacity - once full, no more tickets are sold for the rest of the day and family members cannot join a party already inside. Third-party guides (2026) say it fills before noon on summer weekends and recommend arriving before the 9 a.m. opening; the 11 a.m. typical fill time is an estimate from those reports.
parks.description: The classic mermaid-show attraction on Florida's Nature Coast, where Buccaneer Bay adds a white-sand beach, a lazy river and two water slides that drop into the first-magnitude spring. It is the only lifeguarded spring in this list, and it sells out on summer weekends.

parks.name: Kelly Park / Rock Springs
parks.hours: Summer (March to early November) 8 a.m.-8 p.m.; winter (November to March) 8 a.m.-6 p.m. The waterfront and nature trails close one hour before park closing. Concession stand open daily spring break through early October.
parks.fees: $5 per vehicle; $10 per bus (effective Aug 11, 2026). Cash, or Visa/MasterCard/Discover with photo ID. Tube rentals from vendors outside the park; camping extra.

rules.alcohol: Not allowed anywhere on park property (Orange County ordinance).
rules.tubing: Float the 68-72 F Rock Springs Run (about 25 minutes), then a 10-minute walk back on a paved sidewalk - no shuttle. No rentals inside the park: rent from vendors outside or bring your own tube, noodle or float under 5 ft in length or width. No air pump on site.
rules.pets: No pets in the park or campground - ADA service animals only.
rules.life_jackets: Coast Guard-approved life jackets and puddle jumpers are allowed; water wings are not.
other: Everyone must stay out of the cave at the spring head.
Pop-up canopies up to 10 x 10 ft in the picnic area only; no tents at the waterfront; grills only in picnic areas, never near the water.
The swim area closes when the lightning-prediction system triggers, or when lifeguards lose sight of the river bottom.
Get a re-entry stamp at the gatehouse before leaving to fetch tubes or food.

parks.safety_notes: Lifeguards are on stand along the run during peak season only, not year-round - watch children closely. The water is 68-72 F year-round (colder than most springs) and the run is shallow and rocky. The cave at the spring head is off-limits. Alligators and snakes are occasionally seen in the water - tell staff. The swim area closes for lightning.
parks.entrance_notes: 400 E Kelly Park Rd, Apopka (407-254-1902; capacity info line 407-254-1906). Orange County park: 280 vehicles are admitted each morning; once full, the first 50 cars in line get passes for a 1 p.m. re-opening (one pass per car). Officially, on a typical summer day the park is full within an hour of opening, and visitors report lining up from 4:30 a.m. Family members cannot join a party already inside once the park is at capacity. The county web page and info line are updated when the park is full. Wekiwa Springs State Park (reservation-only) is the nearest backup.
parks.description: Orange County's spring-fed tubing run north of Apopka, where a 68-degree spring feeds a shallow, rocky run through the woods to a sandy swim area and picnic lawns. It is the fastest-filling swimming hole in Central Florida, usually closing within an hour of opening on summer weekends.
